extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians (faculty, researchers, graduate students), prospective AMS meeting organizers and attendees, applicants to academic positions and summer schools
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural requirements for participating in AMS meetings and related academic activities (abstract submission, registration, refunds), plus application and ordering instructions appearing in the Notices of the AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRM Summer School application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The summer school will be primarily aimed at PhD students in their final years and recent PhDs. Applications should be sent by March 31, 1996 along with a curriculum vitae and a list of some recent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers listed. Those wishing to participate in the CRM activities are invited to write to Louis Pelletier, CRM, Universite de Montreal, C.P. 6128, succ. Centre-ville, Montreal (Quebec) CANADA H3C 3J7 or e-mail to ACTIVITES@CRM.UMontreal.CA. (Statement of target audience, deadline, and required application materials.)

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS meetings abstract submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential organizers and speakers should refer to the January issue of the Notices for guidelines on participation and abstract submission. Close attention should be paid to specified deadlines in this issue. Unfortunately, late abstracts cannot be accommodated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed electronic abstracts should be submitted to abs-submit@ams.org; requests for general information concerning abstracts may be sent to abs-info@ams.org. Paper abstracts should be sent to the Abstracts Coordinator, AMS Meetings and Conferences Department, P.O. Box 6887, Providence, RI 02940; telephone: 401-455-4182. Any other inquiries about AMS meetings may be sent to meet@ams.org. (Note: an enhanced submission system was announced to begin fall 1996; see April issue for details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS meetings refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual policy is that a 50 percent refund can be made if notice of cancellation is received before the start of the meeting. After the start of the meeting, no refunds can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special exception example: Individuals who registered in advance for the January 1996 Joint Mathematics Meetings in Orlando but were prevented from attending because of severe weather may request a refund of 50 percent of the meeting advance registration fee by writing to the Mathematics Meetings Housing Bureau, P.O. Box 6887, Providence, RI 02940, or by sending e-mail to pop@ams.org. The Committee granted this exception for unusual weather circumstances but stated it will not prejudice application of the usual policy for future meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting registration schedule (example: Meeting #909, Iowa City)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration location and times for the meeting are specified in the program notices: Third floor of the Iowa Memorial Union: Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendees must register at the published times and location for the specified meeting. (This is an example for Meeting #909; other meetings list their own registration locations/times in their program notices.)

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Auckland lectureship applicant qualifications and application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a Doctorate or equivalent, and should have a proven record in research and teaching in some branch of algebra, logic or discrete mathematics. Applications are particularly welcome from candidates with computational experience and/or expertise in fields closely related to the research interest of existing staff in this area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commencing salary will be established within the range NZ$42,500–NZ$51,500 per annum. Further information, Conditions of Appointment and Method of Application should be obtained from the Academic Appointments Office, The University of Auckland, Private Bag 92019, Auckland, New Zealand, phone +64-9-373-7999 ext 5097, fax +64-9-373-7023. Three copies of applications should be forwarded to reach the Registrar by 13 May 1996. Please quote Vacancy Number UAC.695 in all correspondence. The University has an equal opportunities policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NJIT applied mathematics position qualifications and application method
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications include PhD in mathematical sciences and strong commitment to both research and teaching on all levels; academic administrative experience preferred. Areas of departmental expertise and desired research areas are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send resume to: Personnel Box C-Math. For further inquiries contact Prof. David Stickler, Search Committee Chair, Dept. of Mathematics at NJIT. (Posting notes NJIT is an Equal Opportunity Employer/AA.)

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS book ordering, pricing, and shipping terms
rubrics_metrics.description: All prices subject to change. Charges for delivery are $3.00 per order, or for air delivery outside of the continental U.S., include $6.50 per item. Prepayment required. Residents of Canada, please include 7% GST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order from: American Mathematical Society, P.O. Box 5904, Boston, MA 02206-5904. For credit card orders, fax (401) 331-3842 or call toll free 800-321-4AMS (4267) in the U.S. and Canada. Include applicable delivery charges and taxes; contact customer service at cust-serv@ams.org or call toll free 1-800-321-4AMS (4267) in U.S. and Canada, (401) 455-4000 worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birkhauser ordering and territory/pricing notes
rubrics_metrics.description: To order Birkhauser titles: call toll-free 1-800-777-4643 or fax 617-876-1272; your reference number is Y048. Prices are valid in North America only and are subject to change without notice.

For price and ordering information outside North America, contact Birkhauser Verlag AG, P.O. Box 133, Klosterberg 23, CH-4010, Basel, Switzerland. Fax +41 61 271 7666.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathSciNet search fields and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Search through over 50 years of Mathematical Reviews and Current Mathematical Publications data. Identifies all published forms of an author's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathSciNet search options include: Author, Title, Review text, Journal, Series, Mathematics Subject Classification number, Mathematical Reviews number, Reviewer's name, Publication year, All of the above (a Boolean search narrows results). For more information visit the AMS e-MATH home page or contact cust-serv@ams.org or call toll free 1-800-321-4AMS (4267) in the U.S. and Canada, (401) 455-4000 worldwide.
